proposed_widenings.name: passive ClassFeatureMechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: Beast Spells has no activation event, no use count, and no reset cadence. It is permanently active whenever Wild Shape is active. The only existing ClassFeatureMechanics family is 'activation', which mandates activationCost + resource (UseCountResource) + resetCadence — none of which apply to this feature. A 'passive' family is needed for always-on class features that modify capabilities without any activation gate.
proposed_widenings.evidence: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form — no 'you can use this feature' phrasing, no once-per-rest limit, no action cost.

proposed_widenings.name: lift_form_restriction (or: modify_spellcasting_restriction)
proposed_widenings.justification: The feature's effect is granting permission to cast spells while in Beast form, with a carved-out exception for costly/consumed Material components. This is not 'grant_extra_action' or 'heal_hp'. It is a conditional permission modifier on the caster's spellcasting ability that applies within a specific form-state. No v4 effect atom covers 'remove restriction on spellcasting in a specific creature form'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component

notes: The structural gap is unambiguous: ClassFeatureMechanicsHeader mandates resource + resetCadence, which are inapplicable to a passive always-on feature. Forcing this into the activation family with fake resource fields (use_count: 1, short_or_long_rest) would produce a provably false trace — the feature has no resource to consume and never 'resets'. Both the missing family and the missing effect type are needed before this unit can be encoded honestly.
